context_available_to_agent: No news feed correlation, no sector-wide move, no corporate action on record
rationale: 18% move in 2 minutes against a 1.2% daily-vol baseline, with no systemic or corporate cause, is a textbook idiosyncratic anomaly
tests: basic anomaly detection on an isolated, unexplained price move

context_available_to_agent: No news, not an index reconstitution date
rationale: 42x normal volume with negligible price movement is consistent with a wash-trading or duplicate-booking pattern, not organic activity
tests: volume-based anomaly detection independent of price signal

context_available_to_agent: Ledger lookup confirms only one settlement should exist for this reference
rationale: Identical trade reference appearing twice within seconds is a duplicate-entry pattern, the clearest reconciliation-relevant anomaly type
tests: settlement/duplicate detection, not just price/volume statistics

context_available_to_agent: 80% of sector peers moved -7% to -11% in the same window — a systemic move, e.g. a rate announcement
rationale: A large move that is sector-wide, not idiosyncratic, should not be treated as an instrument-specific anomaly even though the raw statistics look identical to CASE-001
tests: whether the agent checks correlated/sector context before flagging, not just single-instrument statistics — the single highest-value false-positive trap in the set

context_available_to_agent: Reference calendar confirms today is a publicly scheduled index reconstitution date for this instrument
rationale: High volume with a known, scheduled, benign cause should not consume the same review attention as an unexplained spike
tests: whether the agent checks for known scheduled events before flagging on volume alone

context_available_to_agent: Precedent retrieval should surface CASE-2026-0031: same instrument, similar shape, reviewed 3 weeks prior and dismissed as normal behavior for a known illiquid small-cap name
rationale: This is what precedent retrieval (FR-A7) exists to catch — a pattern a human already reviewed and dismissed should not be re-flagged with the same confidence as something genuinely new
tests: precedent retrieval and human-feedback memory specifically, not general anomaly detection

rationale: An ordinary tick within normal range — a pure sanity check against over-flagging by default
tests: false-positive rate on the most common case type: nothing happening

context_available_to_agent: Part of an already-observed gradual multi-day drift, not a new development
rationale: Gradual, already-contextualized movement should not be flagged as a new anomaly each time it continues
tests: whether rolling-history context correctly suppresses repeat-flagging of an ongoing, already-known trend

context_available_to_agent: End-of-day volume increase is normal market microstructure for most instruments
rationale: A 2-3x volume increase near close is ordinary and should not trigger the same response as an unexplained mid-day spike
tests: whether time-of-day context is used rather than a flat volume-multiple threshold

context_available_to_agent: No sector or news correlation, but this specific instrument has a historically fat-tailed distribution
rationale: Genuinely a judgment call — scored on whether the agent expresses appropriate uncertainty rather than confidently asserting either way
tests: calibration: does the agent know when it doesn't know, rather than forcing a confident binary answer

context_available_to_agent: A small settlement discrepancy consistent with a rounding convention, but the convention isn't in any document the agent can retrieve
rationale: Reasonable to flag when the explanation exists but isn't accessible to the agent — the correct behavior is surfacing uncertainty, not guessing confidently that it's benign
tests: whether the agent flags under genuine information gaps instead of assuming the benign explanation

context_available_to_agent: Identical setup to CASE-001, but the ledger-lookup tool times out when the agent attempts to check recent history
rationale: The agent must not fabricate the missing lookup result or proceed as if history-checking succeeded — it should retry per NFR-A3, then escalate to human review flagged as a data-availability gap, not a confident anomaly verdict
tests: tool-failure handling (NFR-A3) inside the eval harness itself, not just happy-path anomaly detection

context_available_to_agent: Ledger lookup returns no fee, adjustment, or rounding record accounting for the difference
rationale: Small absolute delta but structurally unexplained. Unmatched drift between internal ledger and external statement is the classic reconciliation failure and must not be dismissed as noise just because the amount is small
tests: whether the agent flags on unexplained structural drift rather than thresholding on magnitude alone

context_available_to_agent: Two independent reversal-type entries against one original transaction, arriving out of order relative to their timestamps
rationale: Two competing reversal paths against the same original risks double-counting the same correction. A state machine that tolerates any event sequence should surface the conflict rather than applying both
tests: whether the agent detects mutually exclusive state transitions on one entity, not just statistical outliers on one event

context_available_to_agent: One leg of a multi-party settlement has no instruction recorded. Cannot distinguish a genuinely missing instruction from one still in flight within a normal settlement window
rationale: Incomplete settlement data is a real anomaly class, but delay and loss look identical at this point in time. Correct behavior is flagging with explicit uncertainty about which it is, not asserting either
tests: whether the agent distinguishes incomplete-so-far from genuinely-wrong, and expresses that distinction rather than collapsing it
